scenes.title: Fear and Pity from the Plot
scenes.summary: The better poet raises fear and pity from the plot itself, so that one who only hears the story of Oedipus shudders; the merely monstrous has no part in tragedy.

scenes.title: Within the Family
scenes.summary: The pitiable deeds are those among people dear to each other: brother against brother, son against father, mother against son.

scenes.title: Knowing and Not Knowing
scenes.summary: The traditional stories must be kept, Clytemnestra killed by Orestes and Eriphyle by Alcmaeon, but well used: the deed may be done knowingly, like Medea's, in ignorance, like Oedipus' or Telegonus', or prevented by recognition.

scenes.title: The Ranking
scenes.summary: Worst is to know and not to act, as Haemon with Creon; then to act knowing; better, to act in ignorance; best, recognition just in time: Merope in the Cresphontes, Iphigenia and her brother, the Helle.

scenes.title: Why So Few Houses
scenes.summary: The poets found such plots by chance and keep returning to the houses in which such sufferings happened.
